name: Power Plugs & Voltage
description: Malta uses Type G plugs (3 rectangular pins, UK style). Voltage is 230V (50Hz). US travelers need a plug adapter. For high-draw appliances (hair dryers), a voltage converter is needed unless the device is dual-voltage.
notes: Laptops and phone chargers are usually dual-voltage (100-240V), so only a physical adapter is required.

name: Currency & Tipping
description: The currency is the Euro (€). Credit cards are widely accepted (Visa/Mastercard). Tipping is usually 5-10% at restaurants if a service charge is not already included on the bill.
notes: Always carry a small amount of cash (Euro coins) for small purchases or buses.

name: Language
description: Maltese and English are the official languages. English is spoken fluently by the vast majority of the population.
notes: US travelers will have zero language barrier.

name: SIM / eSIM Options
description: Local providers are Epic, GO, and Melita. For a US traveler, downloading an eSIM (like Airalo or Holafly) before departure is the easiest way to have data upon landing.
notes: Ensure your US phone is carrier-unlocked before trying to use an eSIM.

name: Health & Emergency
description: Emergency number is 112. Tap water is safe to drink, but is often desalinated so locals and tourists frequently prefer bottled water for taste.

name: October Weather
description: Mid-October (during the event) sees pleasant weather with average highs around 24-25°C (75-77°F) and lows around 17-18°C (63-64°F).
notes: Pack light layers; a light jacket is good for the evening.
